title: Sell Mineral Rights in Orin, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Orin, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Orin, Converse County, in the middle of the Powder River Basin's Niobrara and Turner Sand drilling? Get a real number.
heroLead: Orin sits along the North Platte in Converse County, close to the junction where the old rail line meets some of the busiest horizontal drilling ground in the Powder River Basin.
intro: Converse County has been the epicenter of Powder River Basin horizontal development for years now, with operators running long laterals through the Niobrara and Turner Sand and, in places, stacking multiple benches under the same surface acreage. Orin's location along the North Platte corridor puts it in reach of that development, and mineral interests here can range from actively producing horizontal units to acreage still waiting on a permit.

The old railroad junction here gave the community its start, and some of the surrounding sections still carry the private mineral title that came out of the original grant, distinct from federal ground nearby.

sections.heading: Stacked-pay horizontal development
paragraphs: What makes Converse County acreage different from an older Wyoming field is the stacked-pay approach — operators sometimes hold rights to drill multiple formations under the same surface tract, meaning your mineral interest could be tied to more than one producing well over time as different benches get developed. We check which formation and which specific well your interest is actually in before pricing it, since a Niobrara unit and a Turner unit under the same section can look completely different on paper.

sections.heading: Railroad-era checkerboard nearby
paragraphs: This stretch of Converse County carries some of the old Union Pacific railroad grant checkerboard pattern, with private and federal sections alternating. If your acreage traces back to that grant, confirming clean private title versus BLM-administered minerals matters before any sale can close.

sections.heading: What we need
paragraphs: A division order or check stub naming your well and decimal interest is the fastest path. If your acreage is undeveloped, the legal description lets us check current permitting activity nearby.

faqs.question: My royalty checks come from more than one well on the same land — is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's typical of stacked-pay development in Converse County, where multiple formations under the same acreage can each support separate wells over time.

faqs.question: How do I know if my section is federal or private minerals?
faqs.answer: We check your legal description against the historic railroad grant pattern and BLM records to confirm.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests in acreage that's permitted but not yet drilled?
faqs.answer: We evaluate that case by case, weighted on how close the permit is to becoming an actual well.

faqs.question: Why does the railroad grant matter for my interest near Orin?
faqs.answer: It determines whether your section is private mineral title or federal BLM ground, which changes how — or whether — we can buy it.
